quiz.prompt: A model asks to `Read` "../outside.txt". What does the host policy do?

options.text: Allows it because `Read` is on the allowlist.
options.explanation: The tool is allowed, but the path must also pass `inside()`.

options.text: Asks the model to confirm the path is safe.
options.explanation: The model's confirmation is not authority; the host decides.

options.text: It ends the whole Python process.
options.explanation: Only the single tool call is refused; the run can continue.

options.text: It deletes the requested file.
options.explanation: A denial performs no action on the file.

options.text: `create_sdk_mcp_server(name="lesson", tools=[add])`
options.explanation: Correct. It wraps the decorated functions in an SDK MCP server that you place in `mcp_servers`.

options.text: `ClaudeSDKClient.add_tool(add)`
options.explanation: This method does not exist on `ClaudeSDKClient`.

options.text: `query(tools=[add])`
options.explanation: `query()` takes `prompt` and `options`; custom tools go through `mcp_servers`.

quiz.prompt: Why does the tool call `Calculation.model_validate` even though the schema is sent to the model?

options.text: Because the SDK deletes the schema after the first call.
options.explanation: The schema stays registered; the issue is trust, not deletion.

options.text: Because Pydantic makes the arithmetic faster.
options.explanation: Validation is about safety, not speed.

options.text: Because model-generated arguments are untrusted input that may break the schema.
options.explanation: Correct. The host enforces types, bounds and forbidden extra fields itself.

quiz.prompt: Which input does `Calculation` accept?

options.explanation: Strict mode rejects booleans; this is one of the three rejected cases.
Correct. Integers are valid for float fields even in strict mode, and both are within bounds.
`extra="forbid"` rejects the unknown `shell` field.

concept_brief: `ClaudeSDKClient` keeps one conversation open: inside `async with ClaudeSDKClient(options=...) as client` you call `await client.query(...)`, consume `client.receive_response()`, then send the next turn on the same client so context is retained.
lab_brief: The offline exercise `sessions` builds the ordered two-turn plan (the lesson prompt, then the follow-up) and lists the client lifecycle the live run follows. It makes the turn order and connection ownership explicit before any model is involved.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open this lesson in the browser.
Live (optional): put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env, then restart the server so the Live Agent SDK mode appears.
The Follow-up for conversation lessons field is only editable in live mode; offline uses the default follow-up.

quiz.prompt: Why does the live run send both turns on the same `ClaudeSDKClient`?

options.text: Because `query()` cannot send text.
options.explanation: `query()` can send a prompt, but each call starts a new session; it is not about sending text.

options.text: So the second turn shares the first turn's conversation context.
options.explanation: Correct. One open client keeps the session, so the follow-up can refer to the earlier answer.

options.text: Because two clients would double the budget threshold.
options.explanation: The budget is per run option; sharing context is the reason.

quiz.prompt: What should happen after the last `receive_response()` loop finishes?

options.text: The client disconnects in the same task that opened it, which `async with` handles.
options.explanation: Correct. Leaving the `async with` block closes the connection in the owning task.

options.text: The client must stay open until the process exits.
options.explanation: Leaving it open leaks a CLI process and connection.

options.text: You call `client.interrupt()` to close it.
options.explanation: `interrupt()` stops an in-progress response; it is not the disconnect step.

concept_brief: A `PreToolUse` hook is an async callback registered with `HookMatcher` in `ClaudeAgentOptions.hooks`. It receives the tool name and input before the tool runs and can return `permissionDecision` `allow` or `deny` with a reason.

quiz.prompt: When does a PreToolUse hook run?

options.text: After the tool returns its result.
options.explanation: That is PostToolUse; PreToolUse runs before execution.

options.text: Before the tool executes, with the tool name and input.
options.explanation: Correct. It can allow or deny the call before any effect happens.

options.text: Only when the model finishes the conversation.
options.explanation: Stop hooks run at the end; tool hooks run around each tool call.

quiz.prompt: How does a PreToolUse hook block a call?

options.text: It returns hookSpecificOutput with permissionDecision deny and a reason.
options.explanation: Correct. The reason is reported back so the model can adjust.

options.text: It raises an exception inside the tool.
options.explanation: Raising is a failure, not a policy decision; return an explicit deny.

options.text: It edits the system prompt.
options.explanation: Prompts influence the model but do not enforce anything on the host.

Live (optional): put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env, then restart the server so the Live Agent SDK mode appears.

steps.title: Understand the goal

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Open the Python source tab and read the `AgentDefinition(...)` call; note that only `description`, `prompt` and `tools` are set.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Keep Offline Python exercise selected and click Run exercise; the result appears under Response and results with the LOCAL PYTHON RESULT badge.

steps.text: Confirm `reviewer.tools` is Read, Glob and Grep, the other fields are null, and `delegation_tool` is "Agent".

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Build your own `AgentDefinition` with a narrower tool list and a model, and compare its dict.

inspect: Look at `reviewer` (description, prompt, tools and the null fields such as `model`, `maxTurns`, `permissionMode`), `delegation_tool` and `host_authority`.
expected: `reviewer.description` is "Read-only Python lesson reviewer", `reviewer.tools` is ["Read", "Glob", "Grep"], fields such as `model`, `disallowedTools` and `permissionMode` are null, `delegation_tool` is "Agent" and `host_authority` says a role description does not override tool permissions.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms a reviewer definition was produced and that delegation goes through the `Agent` tool.
challenge: In a scratch script, create `AgentDefinition(description="Reader", prompt="Read notes.txt.", tools=["Read"], model="haiku")` and print `dataclasses.asdict(...)`. Verify `tools` is only ["Read"] and `model` is "haiku", while the unset fields stay `None`.
hints: `AgentDefinition` is a dataclass in `claude_agent_sdk`, so `dataclasses.asdict` works on it.
Its other optional fields include `disallowedTools`, `maxTurns`, `effort` and `permissionMode`; leaving them unset means they inherit or use defaults.
reference: The reviewer is configuration, not a running agent: a description the main agent uses to choose it, a prompt, and a tool list. Restricting `tools` to Read, Glob and Grep is what keeps it read-only, not the words "Do not edit files". In live mode the definition is passed in `agents` and the main agent needs the `Agent` tool to delegate to it, while the host policy still checks every call.
recovery: If the run fails, read the red error message and open Diagnostics — raw events; if the offline run itself fails, run `uv sync --locked` again and restart `uv run agent-lab serve`.

If Live Agent SDK is not offered or reports an authentication error, check that .env has an Anthropic `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true, then restart the server; the offline exercise is complete without it. In live mode the subagent appears only if the main agent chooses to call the `Agent` tool.

concept_brief: `query()` accepts an async iterable instead of a string. Each item is a user-message dict (`type`, `message`, `parent_tool_use_id`, `session_id`), produced lazily; the CLI answers each one as a queued turn. Token streaming of the reply is the separate `include_partial_messages` option.
lab_brief: The `streaming` exercise builds user messages with the `user_messages` async generator and streams them through the SDK's real `query()` to the scripted CLI, which answers each message as its own turn. Live runs use the same generator. The offline run uses the real SDK client code against `ScriptedCLI` (`agent_lab/scripted_cli.py`), a scripted stand-in for the Claude Code process: no model is called.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 12 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 12`).
Live (optional): set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE=true` in `.env`, then restart the app. The live run streams your prompt and the follow-up as two turns.

concept_brief: An MCP server exposes typed tools over a transport. With stdio, the client starts the server as a subprocess and exchanges JSON-RPC messages on its stdin and stdout; `ClaudeAgentOptions.mcp_servers` takes the same command for live runs.

challenge: In a scratch script, create `Budget(limit=0.10)`, record 0.05, call `before_call(0.03)` (it passes), record 0.03, then call `before_call(0.03)` again. Verify the second check raises `ValueError: Host budget exhausted; no new call may start.` and that `record(-1)` raises `Invalid actual cost.`.
hints: `from agent_lab.services import Budget`; the rule is `spent + reserve >= limit` means no new call.

concept_brief: Orchestrating several agents is host work: validate a plan, run independent tasks concurrently with `asyncio.TaskGroup` bounded by an `asyncio.Semaphore`, and start a task only after its dependencies finish. File ownership, unknown dependencies and cycles are rejected before any worker starts.

Then give two tasks the same file and look for 'More than one owner'.
hints: A wave is every task whose dependencies are all finished.

`waves()` repeatedly collects ready tasks; if none are ready but tasks remain, it raises 'Dependency cycle.'. `execute_plan` runs each wave in an `asyncio.TaskGroup`, so one failing worker cancels its siblings and later waves never start.
reference: T1 has no dependencies, so it forms the first wave; T2 and T3 both depend only on T1, so they run together in the second wave, limited to two at a time by the semaphore. The workers are scripted host functions, not Claude, and each owns a distinct src/*.py file. Because waves run inside `asyncio.TaskGroup`, a failure stops the plan instead of letting dependent tasks run on missing work.

options.text: Because the model decided they were independent.
options.explanation: No model is involved; the host computes waves from `depends_on`.

options.text: Because `max_parallel` is 2.
options.explanation: The concurrency limit caps how many run at once; it does not decide which tasks are ready.

concept_brief: Agent teams exchange messages through a channel the host owns. The board checks sender and recipient membership, limits message length and count, records who sent what, and marks every message as untrusted data, so one agent's text never becomes another agent's instructions.
lab_brief: The `board` exercise creates a `Board` for T1, T2 and lead, sends two handoff messages (T1 to T2, then T2 to lead) and returns them with their provenance and the host bounds of 6 messages per sender and 600 characters.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 56 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 56` in a terminal).

Live (optional): put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env and restart the app. The live `exercise` profile gives Claude one read-only tool, `inspect_exercise`, that returns this run's local evidence.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Learn how a host-owned message board keeps inter-agent messaging bounded and traceable.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Read the `Board` class in `agent_lab/services.py` and predict what `send` does with an unknown member or a seventh message.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Keep the mode on Offline Python exercise and click Run exercise. The badge LOCAL PYTHON RESULT confirms that no prompt was sent to Claude.

steps.title: Verify the evidence
steps.text: Confirm two messages with sender, recipient, text and `trust` 'untrusted data', and `host_bounds` of 6 and 600.

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Break the bounds on purpose with your own `Board` and read the errors.

inspect: The `messages` table (sender, recipient, text, trust) and the `host_bounds` group.
expected: Two messages: T1 to T2 '`normalize_tag`(value: str) -> str is ready.' and T2 to lead 'Search imports the completed normalization function.', both with trust 'untrusted data'. `host_bounds` shows `per_sender` 6 and characters 600.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms that the team handoff messages were recorded and the host bounds were reported.
challenge: Run `uv run python -c "from agent_lab.services import Board; b=Board({'T1','lead'}); [b.send('T1','lead','ok') for _ in range(6)]; b.send('T1','lead','one more')"` and confirm 'Message limit exceeded.'. Then try `b.send('T9','lead','hi')` and confirm 'Unknown board member.'.
hints: Provenance comes from the host's `send` call, not from anything written inside the message text.
`send` rejects unknown members, empty text, text over 600 characters and a seventh message from the same sender, then stores sender, recipient, text and trust 'untrusted data'.
reference: Each message records who sent it and to whom, so the lead can trace a handoff back to its author. The board, not the agents, enforces membership and limits, which stops one agent from flooding or impersonating another. Labelling messages as untrusted data reminds receivers to treat them as evidence rather than commands.
recovery: If the run fails, read the first error in the panel, run `uv run agent-lab lesson 56` in a terminal to see every event, and run `uv run agent-lab doctor` if the SDK or CLI looks missing.

quiz.prompt: Why is every board message marked 'untrusted data'?

options.text: Because the messages are encrypted.
options.explanation: Nothing is encrypted; the label is about authority, not secrecy.

options.text: Because the board failed to verify them.
options.explanation: The board did verify membership and limits; the label still applies to the content.

options.text: Because another agent's text must be treated as evidence, never as instructions that grant authority.
options.explanation: Correct. This limits prompt injection travelling from one agent to the next.

quiz.prompt: What happens when T1 tries to send a seventh message?

options.text: `send` raises ValueError 'Message limit exceeded.'.
options.explanation: Correct. The host caps each sender at 6 messages.

options.text: The oldest message is deleted to make room.
options.explanation: The board never rewrites history; it rejects the new message.

options.text: The message is delivered but flagged.
options.explanation: Over-limit messages are not stored at all.

concept_brief: Parallel coding agents need isolated working copies: each worker gets its own `git worktree` and branch from one repository, and the host runs operations that touch shared repository state one at a time. A live SDK worker would get `ClaudeAgentOptions(cwd=...)` pointing at its own worktree.
lab_brief: The `worktrees` exercise creates a disposable repository in the run workspace, makes an empty commit on main, then adds worktrees T1 and T2 on new branches by awaiting `git` subprocesses one after another with a 15-second timeout. It returns `git worktree list --porcelain` and confirms that no remote was contacted.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 57 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 57` in a terminal).
Install Git and make sure `git --version` works in the same terminal that starts the app; no remote or account is needed.

Live (optional): put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env and restart the app. The live `exercise` profile gives Claude one read-only tool, `inspect_exercise`, that returns this run's local evidence.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Learn how worktrees isolate parallel workers and why shared repository operations are serialized.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Read `worktrees` in `agent_lab/exercises.py`: note that each `await git(...)` finishes before the next starts.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Keep the mode on Offline Python exercise and click Run exercise. The badge LOCAL PYTHON RESULT confirms that no prompt was sent to Claude.

steps.title: Verify the evidence
steps.text: Find three worktree blocks (repo on main, T1 on refs/heads/T1, T2 on refs/heads/T2) sharing one HEAD commit, and `remote_operations` No.

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Run the lesson twice and compare the paths, or reproduce the worktrees by hand in an empty folder.

inspect: The `worktrees` list (lines starting with `worktree`, `HEAD` and `branch`) and `remote_operations`.
expected: `worktrees` shows `worktree .../work/repo` with `branch refs/heads/main`, `worktree .../work/T1` with `branch refs/heads/T1` and `worktree .../work/T2` with `branch refs/heads/T2`, all with the same HEAD hash. `remote_operations` is No.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms that the worktree list was produced and that no remote operation took place.
challenge: Run the lesson twice: the paths change because each run gets a fresh workspace, but the branch lines stay the same. Then in an empty folder run `git init -b main`, `git commit --allow-empty -m x`, `git worktree add -b T3 ../T3` and `git worktree list` to reproduce a third isolated worker.
hints: A worktree is a second checkout of the same repository on its own branch.

All workers share one .git directory, so commands like `worktree add` change shared state; the exercise awaits them sequentially rather than in parallel. The `-c core.longpaths=true` option avoids Windows path-length failures.
reference: The host created one repository and two extra worktrees, each on its own branch from the same commit, so workers can edit files without touching each other's checkout. Repository-wide operations ran one at a time to avoid races on shared Git state. Everything stayed local: no remote was added, fetched or pushed.
recovery: If the error says 'Install Git to run the worktree lesson.', install Git, restart the terminal and the app, and check `git --version`. If a 'Git fixture operation failed' message mentions paths, move the repo to a shorter folder.

quiz.prompt: Why does each worker get its own worktree?

options.text: To make Git commands run faster.
options.explanation: Speed is not the goal; isolation is.

options.text: So each worker edits its own checkout and branch without overwriting another worker's files.
options.explanation: Correct. Worktrees give isolated working directories that share one repository history.

options.text: Because the SDK cannot work in the main checkout.
options.explanation: The SDK can use any `cwd`; separation is a coordination choice.

quiz.prompt: Why does the exercise await each `git worktree add` before starting the next?

options.text: Because these commands change shared repository state in .git, and running them concurrently could race.
options.explanation: Correct. Shared state is serialized while workers stay parallel in their own folders.

options.text: Because asyncio cannot run subprocesses in parallel.
options.explanation: It can; the exercise chooses not to for shared state.

options.text: Because Git requires a network round trip for each worktree.
options.explanation: Worktrees are local; `remote_operations` is false.

concept_brief: Model routing picks a model and limits per task with explicit host rules: simple tasks go to a fast model with tight limits, complex ones to a more capable model with a larger turn and budget allowance.

preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 59 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 59`).
Optional: set `LAB_ROUTE_MODEL` in `.env` to choose the capable tier's model; routing itself makes no model call.

options.explanation: Correct. Limits follow the expected work.

options.text: The SDK requires different limits per model.
options.explanation: The SDK does not require that; it is a cost decision.

concept_brief: A durable agent records each completed step in an append-only journal (flushed and fsynced) with an idempotency key, and on restart replays the journal and skips finished steps so side effects are not repeated. SDK session resume restores the conversation, not your application's side effects.
lab_brief: The `durable` exercise runs the steps prepare, compute and verify, then runs the same loop a second time as if resuming after an interruption. The second pass finds every step in `journal.completed()` and does nothing, so each side effect happens exactly once.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 60 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 60` in a terminal).

Live (optional): put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env and restart the app. The live `exercise` profile gives Claude one read-only tool, `inspect_exercise`, that returns this run's local evidence.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Learn how journaling, replay and idempotency keys make a long-running job safe to resume.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Read the `Journal` class in `agent_lab/services.py` and `durable` in `agent_lab/exercises.py`; predict the effects after two passes.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Keep the mode on Offline Python exercise and click Run exercise. The badge LOCAL PYTHON RESULT confirms that no prompt was sent to Claude.

steps.title: Verify the evidence
steps.text: Expand Journal: three `completed` rows with matching idempotency keys. Confirm `effects` has three steps and `resume_duplicates` is No.

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Simulate a crash after the first step and confirm that resuming runs only the remaining steps.

expected: `journal` has three rows (completed prepare, compute and verify, each with the same `idempotency_key`). `effects` is prepare, compute, verify, listed once each, `resume_duplicates` is No and `note` recommends an external transactional outbox.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms that the journal recorded the completed steps and that resuming did not repeat any side effect.
challenge: Write a short script with `Journal(Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'j.jsonl')`, append `{'event':'completed','step':'prepare','idempotency_key':'prepare'}` to simulate a crash after step one, then run the same skip-if-completed loop. Confirm the effects are ['compute', 'verify'] and the journal has 3 rows.
hints: The loop checks the journal before doing each step, not after.

`Journal.append` writes one JSON line, flushes and calls `os.fsync`; `completed()` replays the file and returns the finished step names. A crash between doing the side effect and journaling it could still repeat it, which is why the note recommends a transactional outbox.
reference: The first pass performed and journaled all three steps; the second pass replayed the journal, saw every step completed and skipped them, so `effects` has no duplicates. Writing the journal durably before moving on is what makes the resume safe. The remaining gap, a crash between the side effect and its journal entry, needs an outbox or an idempotent downstream system.
recovery: If the run fails, read the first error in the panel, run `uv run agent-lab lesson 60` in a terminal to see every event, and run `uv run agent-lab doctor` if the SDK or CLI looks missing.

If live mode is unavailable or rejects your key, stay offline: the local evidence and the automatic check are the same. Fix `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env, restart the app, then try live again.

quiz.prompt: Why is `effects` only three items long after two passes?

options.text: Because the second pass replays the journal and skips steps already marked completed.
options.explanation: Correct. The completed check runs before each step, so finished work is not repeated.

options.text: Because the second pass crashed.
options.explanation: It ran normally and simply found nothing left to do.

options.text: Because Python deduplicates lists automatically.
options.explanation: Lists keep duplicates; the journal check prevents them.

quiz.prompt: What risk does the note about a transactional outbox address?

options.text: The journal file growing too large.
options.explanation: Size is not the issue described.

options.text: A crash after the side effect happens but before it is journaled, which would repeat it on resume.
options.explanation: Correct. An outbox records the intent and the effect atomically so neither is lost or doubled.

options.text: The model forgetting the conversation.
options.explanation: Conversation state is handled by SDK sessions; the journal protects side effects.

concept_brief: You can expose an agent as an MCP tool: the outer MCP client calls a typed tool whose async handler starts an inner Agent SDK run. The inner run keeps its own limits and gates, whatever the outer client asks.
lab_brief: The `agent_mcp` exercise connects an MCP client to `build_server` in `agent_lab/integrations/agent_mcp.py` with live access forced off, lists the typed tool and calls it. The call travels through MCP into `RunService`, which refuses the paid run.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 61 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 61`).
To serve it for real: `uv run python -m agent_lab.integrations.agent_mcp` with live access enabled (paid).

Retrieved text comes back as tool-result data labelled as evidence, never as system prompt instructions.
lab_brief: The offline `retrieval` exercise calls `retrieve()` from `agent_lab/services.py` on a three-passage policy corpus, scoring passages by shared words, for a real query and an unrelated one. It shows bounded results with citation ids and an empty list when nothing matches, which stops the model from citing an irrelevant passage.
preparation: Run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open http://127.0.0.1:8080/?lesson=62. Offline mode needs nothing else.
Optional live mode: put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env, then restart the server and choose Live Agent SDK.

steps.text: Return a small, cited set of evidence and keep source text separate from instructions.

steps.text: Query a different policy from a scratch script and check which id comes back.

inspect: Look at `query`, the `evidence` table (id, text, score, trust), `unknown_topic` and `citation_rule`.
expected: `query` is "refunds requested"; `evidence` has one row: id refunds#1, text "Refunds may be requested within 30 days of delivery.", score 2, trust "source evidence, not instructions". `unknown_topic` (for "lunar rover") shows None, and `citation_rule` says to cite the evidence id.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms the refund query returned cited evidence and the run reported its citation rule.

challenge: Run `uv run python -c "from agent_lab.services import retrieve; print(retrieve('password reset'))"`. You should get one result, security#1 with score 2. In live mode, ask "Use the `search_policy` tool to find how long password reset links last" and check the answer cites security#1.

`retrieve()` splits the query and each passage into lowercase words, scores the overlap, sorts by score, keeps at most `limit` (3) rows and drops rows scoring 0, then adds the `trust` label.
reference: Only refunds#1 shares words with "refunds requested", so it is the only evidence returned, with an id the model can cite. lab_brief: The offline `analysis` exercise reads the seeded sales.csv with `csv.DictReader`, sums `amount` by `region` and records a computation ledger. The numbers are computed by code, so the model cannot get them wrong when it explains them.
preparation: Run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open http://127.0.0.1:8080/?lesson=71. Offline mode needs nothing else.
Optional live mode: put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env, then restart the server and choose Live Agent SDK.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Compute results in Python and attach a ledger that says how they were computed.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Add a new computed metric to the exercise and record it in the ledger.

inspect: Look at `rows`, `totals` (north, south), `grand_total`, the `ledger` entry and `computed_by`.
expected: `rows` 3, `totals` north 160 and south 80, `grand_total` 240, a `ledger` entry {operation sum, column amount, `group_by` region, source sales.csv} and `computed_by` "Python host, not the model".
evidence_criterion: The check confirms Python read 3 rows and computed a grand total of 240.
challenge: In your copy of `analysis`, also count rows per region and return `"averages": {region: totals[region] / counts[region]}` with a second ledger entry `{"operation": "mean", ...}`. Run again and check north and south both average 80.0. In live mode, ask Claude to explain the totals and check it quotes 240 from the tool.
hints: The input is three rows: north 120, south 80, north 40.
Keep a `counts` dict next to `totals` inside the same loop, divide after the loop, and append a ledger dict describing the new operation so a reader can audit it.

The live model receives these numbers through `analyze_sales` and only explains them, so any total it reports can be checked against the ledger. Models are good at narrative and unreliable at arithmetic over raw files.

quiz.prompt: In this lab, who computes the sales totals?

options.text: Claude, by reading sales.csv with the Read tool.
options.explanation: No. The live profile gives no Read tool; it only exposes `analyze_sales`.

options.text: The model, then Python checks its answer.
options.explanation: No. The order is reversed: Python computes first and the model explains.

options.text: Python on the host, which the evidence states in `computed_by`.
options.explanation: Correct. The totals come from `csv.DictReader` and integer sums, not from model output.

quiz.prompt: What is the computation ledger for?

options.text: Recording which operation, column, grouping and source produced the numbers so they can be audited.
options.explanation: Correct. A reader can reproduce 160, 80 and 240 from the ledger and the CSV.

options.text: Storing the model's reasoning.
options.explanation: No. The ledger is written by Python before the model is involved.

options.text: Tracking API cost.
options.explanation: No. Cost is reported on ResultMessage; the ledger describes the calculation.

concept_brief: An Agent Skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` (name, description and workflow) plus reference files and scripts. Only the name and description are loaded up front; the agent reads the rest when the skill applies. Here the model writes content as a JSON spec and the skill's script owns the Word format.
lab_brief: The `document` exercise installs the repository's `docgen-skills/atmira-docx` skill into `.claude/skills/`, then follows its workflow: write an incident spec, run the exact build command from `SKILL.md`, read the `SPEC ERROR` line, fix the spec and build again. A fixture stands in for the model's spec writing.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 72 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 72`).
Read `docgen-skills/atmira-docx/SKILL.md` and `reference/incident-report.md` before running.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Use a skill's own workflow to turn validated content into a Word document.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Read the skill's `SKILL.md`, then `INCIDENT_SPEC` and `document` in the source.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Run the offline exercise; it runs the build script twice.

steps.title: Verify the evidence
steps.text: Read both `attempts`, then check the `document` headings and table count. Download the .docx below the results.

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Break the spec differently and read the new SPEC ERROR.

inspect: `skill` (name and description, the only parts loaded up front), `workflow_command`, both `attempts` with their `exit_code` and `output`, and `document` (`headings`, `tables`, `bytes`).
expected: Attempt 1 exits 1 with `SPEC ERROR: spec: An incident report starts with an info callout stating severity and status.` Attempt 2 exits 0 with `Built`. The document has the headings Summary, Impact, Timeline, Root cause and Action items, and 2 tables.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms the skill's script rejected the draft, accepted the fixed spec and produced a document with the required sections.
challenge: In `INCIDENT_SPEC`, change the Action items table columns to `["Action", "Owner"]` and drop the date from each row. Run again and read the SPEC ERROR from both attempts.
hints: The incident rules live in the script's validation, not in the model's prompt.
Without a `Due` column the corrected spec fails too, so both attempts print a SPEC ERROR, `document` is null and the automatic check reports Needs review. Restore the column afterwards.
reference: The skill separates content from format: the model only writes a spec, and the script validates it against the house rules and builds the file. Errors come back as one SPEC ERROR line per problem, so the agent can fix them and retry, and the format never depends on the model.
recovery: If the run fails, read the first error in Response and results, fix it, and run again; the Diagnostics panel shows the raw events.
If the build keeps failing, read each SPEC ERROR line; it names the field and the rule that failed.

quiz.prompt: Which part of a skill is loaded before the skill is used?

options.text: Its name and description from SKILL.md.
options.explanation: Correct. The body, references and scripts are read only when needed.

options.text: Every file in the skill folder.
options.explanation: Loading everything up front would waste context.

options.text: Only the build script.
options.explanation: Scripts run when the workflow calls them.

quiz.prompt: Why does this skill have the model write a JSON spec instead of the .docx?

options.text: JSON files are smaller.
options.explanation: Size is not the reason.

options.text: The script owns format and validation, so documents stay consistent and checkable.
options.explanation: Correct. The model writes content; the script enforces the rules.

options.text: Models cannot write files.
options.explanation: They can; the design keeps format out of the model's hands.

concept_brief: An autonomous reviewer's findings are claims. The host accepts only findings on changed lines in approved files, applies their patches itself, and proves the fix with a test before anything is published.
lab_brief: The `review` exercise writes a buggy `src/tags.py`, filters two recorded findings by changed lines, applies the accepted patch, and runs a real test in a subprocess before and after. The out-of-scope CI file must stay untouched.
preparation: Offline: run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open lesson 73 (or run `uv run agent-lab lesson 73`).
No pull request is published; the exercise works in its own lesson workspace.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Apply only in-scope fixes and prove them with a test.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Read `review`: `changed_lines`, the findings and `run_test`.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Run the offline exercise.

steps.title: Verify the evidence
steps.text: Compare `test_before_patch` with `test_after_patch` and check the CI file.

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Widen the scope and see why the gate exists.

expected: The tags.py finding is accepted and the CI-disabling finding rejected; the test fails before the patch and passes after; `out_of_scope_file_unchanged` is true.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms the test went from failing to passing and the out-of-scope file was not changed.
challenge: Add `".github/workflows/ci.yml": {1}` to `changed_lines`, run again and explain why `out_of_scope_file_unchanged` becomes false. Then restore the scope.
hints: The gate is the only thing standing between a finding and its patch.
Widening the scope accepts the malicious finding, so its patch renames the CI workflow: exactly the change a hostile input wanted.
reference: Scoping findings to changed lines stops a reviewer, or text it read, from steering edits elsewhere. Running the test before and after turns a claimed fix into evidence. Publication stays a separate, human-approved step.
recovery: If the run fails, read the first error in Response and results, fix it, and run again; the Diagnostics panel shows the raw events.
If Live Agent SDK is missing, live mode is disabled: the offline exercise still teaches the full concept without credentials.

quiz.prompt: A finding asks to edit a CI workflow outside the PR's changes. What should the host do?

options.text: Reject it: it is outside the changed lines and approved scope.
options.explanation: Correct. Scope is enforced by the host, not the reviewer.

options.text: Apply it because the severity is high.
options.explanation: Severity does not grant scope.

options.text: Ask the model whether it is safe.
options.explanation: The model may be the one being manipulated.

quiz.prompt: What proves the patch fixed the bug?

options.text: The reviewer says it is fixed.
options.explanation: That is a claim.

options.text: The same test fails before and passes after the patch.
options.explanation: Correct. Before-and-after evidence.

options.text: The patch is short.
options.explanation: Size proves nothing.

concept_brief: Red-teaming tests labelled attack cases against deterministic host boundaries rather than trusting the model to refuse. The `decide()` and `inside()` functions in `agent_lab/policy.py` are the same checks the live `can_use_tool` callback and `PreToolUse` `HookMatcher` use, and `redact()` removes keys and bearer tokens from logged data.
lab_brief: The offline `permission_cases` exercise runs five labelled cases (a normal read, path traversal, a .env read, a Bash command and a Write) through `decide()` and compares each result with its expected outcome. A 1.0 pass rate shows the boundary holds whatever text a prompt injection produces.
preparation: Run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open http://127.0.0.1:8080/?lesson=74. Offline mode needs nothing else.
Optional live mode: put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env, then restart the server and choose Live Agent SDK.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Measure whether host boundaries stop injected tool requests, using cases with known expected outcomes.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Read `decide`, `inside`, `PROTECTED` and `redact` in `agent_lab/policy.py` and `permission_cases` in `agent_lab/exercises.py`.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Keep Offline selected and click Run exercise. The panel shows a LOCAL PYTHON RESULT badge; your prompt is not sent to Claude.

steps.title: Verify the evidence
steps.text: Confirm all five cases passed, `pass_rate` is 1.0 and both redacted values are [REDACTED].

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Add your own attack case and make sure it is denied.

inspect: Look at the `decisions` table (case, tool, allowed, expected, passed, reason), `pass_rate` and `redacted`.
expected: Five rows: normal read allowed; path traversal, secret read, shell injection and unapproved write all denied; every row passed. `pass_rate` 1.0, and `redacted` shows `api_key` and text both as [REDACTED].
evidence_criterion: The check confirms every labelled attack case got its expected decision, for a pass rate of 1.0.
challenge: Add `("glob secrets", "Glob", {"path": ".env"}, False)` and `("git config", "Read", {"file_path": ".git/config"}, False)` to the cases in your copy of `permission_cases`. Run again and check both rows show allowed No and passed Yes, with `pass_rate` still 1.0.
hints: Only Read, Glob and Grep can ever be allowed, and only for paths inside the workspace.
`inside()` resolves the path, requires it to stay under the workspace root and rejects any part in `PROTECTED` (.git, .env, .venv, config, .claude); every other tool name falls through to a deny.
reference: Each case is an input an injected prompt might try, paired with the decision the host must make. All five matched, so the pass rate is 1.0. Because the decision is code, not model judgment, the same result holds in live mode where these checks run inside `can_use_tool` and the PreToolUse hook.
recovery: If the offline run shows an error, read it in the panel and in Diagnostics, then run `uv run agent-lab lesson 74` in a terminal to see the same exercise without the browser.

If Live Agent SDK is missing or fails with an authentication error, keep working offline. Check that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` holds an Anthropic key and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true is in .env, then restart `uv run agent-lab serve`.

quiz.prompt: Why is "shell injection" denied even though the command is harmless `echo preapproved`?

options.text: Because the command text contains a suspicious word.
options.explanation: No. `decide()` does not inspect command text at all.

options.text: Because Bash is not in the read-only lesson policy, so every Bash call is denied.
options.explanation: Correct. Only Read, Glob and Grep can pass; other tools are denied by name.

options.text: Because the model refused it.
options.explanation: No. No model is involved offline; the host decided.

quiz.prompt: What does a red-team pass rate of 1.0 tell you here?

options.text: The model will never follow injected instructions.
options.explanation: No. The cases test host boundaries, not model behavior.

options.text: The app is fully secure.
options.explanation: No. It only covers these labelled cases; add more as new attacks appear.

options.text: Every labelled case got the host decision it was expected to get.
options.explanation: Correct. `pass_rate` is the share of rows where `allowed == expected`.

concept_brief: An autonomous engineering team works when agents propose and the host decides. In live mode `run_live_team` in `agent_lab/engineering.py` runs a lead, two parallel developers and a reviewer through `query()` with `output_format` JSON schemas (`Plan`, `DevelopmentReport`, `TeamReview`); the host validates file ownership and dependencies, checks source with an AST allowlist, runs acceptance tests in an isolated `python -I` subprocess, tracks spend with `Budget` and decides the release gate.
lab_brief: The offline `team` exercise uses scripted Python workers: it validates a three-task `Plan`, runs it in dependency waves with `execute_plan` (TaskGroup, at most 2 in parallel), records `Board` messages and a `Journal`, and runs an acceptance script in a subprocess. It shows the whole control loop, ending in a host release gate and no publication, without any model call.
preparation: Run `uv sync --locked` once, then `uv run agent-lab serve` and open http://127.0.0.1:8080/?lesson=75. Offline mode needs nothing else.
Optional live mode: put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true in .env, then restart the server and choose Live Agent SDK.
Live mode makes six structured agent calls; this lesson's budget threshold is 0.50 USD.

steps.title: Understand the goal
steps.text: Let workers propose code while the host validates ownership, order, tests and release.

steps.title: Prepare your exercise
steps.text: Read `Plan`, `execute_plan`, `Board` and `Journal` in `agent_lab/services.py` and the `team` function in `agent_lab/exercises.py`.

steps.title: Run one example
steps.text: Keep Offline selected and click Run exercise. The panel shows a LOCAL PYTHON RESULT badge; your prompt is not sent to Claude.

steps.title: Verify the evidence
steps.text: Confirm waves [T1] then [T2, T3], all three files compiled, "3 acceptance checks passed", `release_gate` Yes and published No.

steps.title: Try the challenge
steps.text: Feed the plan validator a bad plan and read its rejection.

expected: `plan` T1 owns src/tags.py, T2 src/search.py and T3 src/report.py, both depending on T1; `waves` [T1], [T2, T3]; `workers` "scripted Python fixtures"; each result compiled Yes; three board messages to lead marked "untrusted data"; three journal entries; `release_gate` Yes; `acceptance` "3 acceptance checks passed"; `published` No.
evidence_criterion: The check confirms the acceptance script passed, the host release gate opened and nothing was published.
challenge: In a scratch script build `Plan(tasks=[TaskSpec(id="T1", files=["src/a.py"], depends_on=["T2"]), TaskSpec(id="T2", files=["src/b.py"], depends_on=["T1"])])`: it raises ValidationError "Dependency cycle.". Then give two tasks the same file and confirm "More than one owner for src/a.py."
hints: The Plan model validates itself when constructed, including computing waves.
`validate_graph` rejects duplicate ids, files outside src/*.py, a file with two owners and unknown dependencies, then calls `waves()`, which raises "Dependency cycle." when no task is ready.
reference: The plan was valid, so T1 ran first and T2 and T3 ran in parallel once it finished. Each scripted worker compiled and wrote only its own file, and its board message was marked untrusted. The acceptance subprocess passed all three checks, so the host opened the release gate, but `published` stays false because release still needs a human.
recovery: If a live run fails with a host release-gate or plan error, that is the host doing its job; read the reason, then check the offline run, which uses scripted workers and should always pass.

If Live Agent SDK is missing or fails with an authentication error, keep working offline. Check that `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` holds an Anthropic key and `LAB_ENABLE_LIVE`=true is in .env, then restart `uv run agent-lab serve`.

quiz.prompt: Why do T2 and T3 run in the same wave?

options.text: Both depend only on T1, so they are ready once T1 completes.
options.explanation: Correct. `Plan.waves()` groups all tasks whose dependencies are done, giving [T1] then [T2, T3].

options.text: They edit the same file.
options.explanation: No. The plan validator forbids two owners for one file.

options.text: The model chose to parallelize them.
options.explanation: No. Offline workers are scripted, and waves come from the host's dependency graph.

quiz.prompt: What decides whether the offline release gate opens?

options.text: The developers' board messages saying they compiled.
options.explanation: No. Board messages are marked untrusted data; claims are not evidence.

options.text: The exit code of the isolated acceptance subprocess.
options.explanation: Correct. `release_gate` is `process.returncode == 0` for the acceptance script.

options.text: Whether the code was pushed to GitHub.
options.explanation: No. `published` is always false; this fixture never pushes.

quiz.prompt: In live mode, how does the host stop a developer agent from running arbitrary code?

options.text: It trusts the reviewer agent to catch it.
options.explanation: No. Review happens after acceptance, and a model's approval is not a sandbox.

options.text: It gives the agent Bash but no network.
options.explanation: No. Developers get no tools at all (`tools=[]`); they return source as structured data.

options.text: It checks the proposed source with an AST allowlist before writing or running it.
options.explanation: Correct. `validate_source` permits only approved node types, calls and methods, and rejects files outside the agent's ownership.
